So we make the substitution

$$
u=x^{2} - 20.
$$

Its derivative is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

and we can now write our integral in terms of $u,$ as follows:

$$
\int x\sqrt{x^{2} - 20}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int u^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve the integral in terms of $u$ and then write the final result in terms of $x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int u^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\text{d}u &=\frac{1}{2}\frac{u^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}+C\\ &=\frac{1}{3}u^{\frac{3}{2}}+C\\ &=\frac{\left(x^{2} - 20\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["909bc525-ad6d-5f0b-acd1-9b05c9585d04"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "62d8dfd9-a6bd-508a-9775-552281a549c3"
